docs.title: olymptradeapi
docs.text:
A threading-based Python client for the OlympTrade WebSocket trading API. Same architecture pattern as binomoapi / pocketoptionapi / quotexapi, but built from the ground up against a real wire capture in 2026.

Get started :material-rocket-launch: GitHub :material-github:

docs.title: Why this lib?
docs.text:
• :material-thermometer-low: No async/await — pure threading, drop-in for sync code
  • :material-shield-key: Per-email session storage — multiple accounts, no collisions
  • :material-flash: Auto-refresh — once logged in, captcha-free for 1+ year
  • :material-chart-line: Full coverage — balance, FTT trades, candles, payouts, deal history
  • :material-network: Battle-tested protocol — every endpoint validated against live captures

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
hello.py
from olymptradeapi import OlympTradeAPI

api = OlympTradeAPI(email="you@x.com", password="...", mode="demo")
ok, reason = api.connect()
if not ok:
    print(reason); exit()

# Active-account balance
print(api.get_balance().amount)              # 9787.20

# Place a 15s UP trade on EURUSD_OTC for $1
r = api.buy("EURUSD_OTC", 1, "up", 15)
print("WIN!" if api.check_win(r.deal_id).is_win else "LOSS")

api.logout()

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
┌──────────────────┐
    │  OlympTradeAPI   │  ← user-facing class (stable_api.py)
    └────────┬─────────┘
             │
    ┌────────▼─────────┐
    │  olymptradeapi   │  ← engine — owns sessions + state (api.py)
    └─────┬──────┬─────┘
          │      │
   ┌──────▼──┐ ┌─▼──────────────────┐
   │  httpc/ │ │  ws/client.py      │
   │  ─ Login│ │  threading-based   │
   │  ─ Renew│ │  WS reader + push  │
   │  ─ ...  │ │  dispatcher        │
   └─────────┘ └─┬──────────────────┘
                 │
        ┌────────▼─────────┐
        │  ws/chanels/*.py │  ← one class per outgoing channel
        └──────────────────┘

Same shape as pocketoptionapi. See Protocol overview.

docs.title: What's not in this lib (yet)
docs.text:
• Strategy / indicator framework (use pandas-ta etc.)
  • Real-time tick streaming (e:1)
  • Backtesting

If any of those become useful, they ship as Phase 2 — see the README.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Notable changes to the public API. The earliest commits in the repo (pre-0.3) were rapid iteration; this changelog starts at the v0.3.0 release.

docs.title: v0.3.x — current
docs.text:
• Per-email session storage in <cwd>/olymp_<sha>.dat
  • get_balance() returns the AccountBalance for the active mode (was Balance)
  • get_all_balances() is HTTP-based now (merged with the old get_all_balances_http)
  • change_account() replaces switch_account()
  • OrderResult has clean error_message + error_code fields, concise repr, full_repr() for debug
  • Heartbeat sends e:14 every 25s to keep the WS alive
  • Auto-refresh access_token via gw.olymptrade.com/api/token/renew/web/v1 on saved-session reuse
  • Deal history with cursor pagination + pair filter
  • Profile endpoint wired (api.user_id, api.get_profile())

docs.title: v0.2.x
docs.text:
• Threading rewrite (was async on aiohttp)
  • connect() returns (bool, reason) tuple
  • buy() supports both duration= (timer) and time_close= (clock) modes

docs.title: v0.1.x
docs.text:
• Initial async release
  • HTTP login + WS upgrade
  • e:55 balance handling
  • e:23 buy + check_win()

docs.title: Editable install from source (recommended)
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/mohamedsaid5/olymptradeapi.git
cd olymptradeapi
pip install -e .

-e (editable) means edits to the source take effect on next import — useful while you're customising the lib for your own bot.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
The library has three runtime deps:

  • requests — HTTP login / refresh / accounts / history / profile
  • websocket-client — WS connection + reader thread
  • certifi — bundled root CAs

All three are pulled in automatically by pip install -e ..

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
ImportError: cannot import name 'HTTPStatus' from 'http'

You're running from inside the package directory and a folder named http/ is shadowing the stdlib. Either run from a different cwd, or install the lib with pip install -e . so it imports through site-packages.

WS connection drops immediately after open

The package sets suppress_origin=True to make our explicit Origin: https://olymptrade.com header the only one. If a fork or monkey-patch removes that, the server closes the upgrade. Check ws/client.py if you've forked.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Login → check balance → place a trade → check the outcome → log out. Whole flow.

quick.py
import os
from olymptradeapi import OlympTradeAPI

api = OlympTradeAPI(
    email=os.environ["OLYMPTRADE_EMAIL"],
    password=os.environ["OLYMPTRADE_PASSWORD"],
    mode="demo",
)

ok, reason = api.connect()
if not ok:
    print(f"connect failed: {reason}")
    raise SystemExit

# Balance for the active account
bal = api.get_balance()
print(f"{bal.group}: ${bal.amount:.2f}  id={bal.account_id}")

# Place a $1 UP trade on EURUSD_OTC for 15 seconds
r = api.buy("EURUSD_OTC", amount=1, direction="up", duration=15)
if not r.ok:
    print(f"buy rejected: {r.error_message}")  # e.g. "Not enough real funds"
    api.logout()
    raise SystemExit

print(f"placed deal {r.deal_id} — strike {r.strike_price}, payout {r.winperc}%")

# Block until the deal closes
final = api.check_win(r.deal_id)
verdict = "WIN" if final.is_win else ("LOSS" if final.is_loss else "DRAW")
print(f"verdict: {verdict}  ({final.interim_status})")

api.logout()

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
set OLYMPTRADE_EMAIL=you@x.com
set OLYMPTRADE_PASSWORD=...
python quick.py

Expected output:

demo: $9787.20  id=2746091247
placed deal 12109743450 — strike 1.1808, payout 85.0%
verdict: WIN  (win)

docs.title: Two things this gives you for free
docs.text:
1. Captcha-free subsequent runs

On first login, tokens are saved to <cwd>/olymp_<sha>.dat (encrypted, per-email). The next connect() reuses them — no HTTP login, no captcha risk. See Authentication.

2. Auto-reconnect + heartbeat

A daemon thread sends e:14 every 25s to keep the WS alive, and auto-reconnects on disconnects. Your api.get_balance() reflects the latest server-pushed state at all times.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
OlympTrade has two auth surfaces:

  • HTTP login at /v2/user/login-by-password — captcha-gated after a few attempts
  • HTTP renew at /api/token/renew/web/v1 — not captcha-gated, lasts 1–3 years

The library tries the captcha-free path first, falls back to password only if needed.

docs.title: How connect() resolves auth
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[connect] --> B{access_token<br>passed?}
    B -- yes --> C[try WS upgrade<br>with the token]
    B -- no --> D{saved tokens<br>for this email?}
    D -- yes --> C
    D -- no --> E[HTTP login with<br>email + password]
    E -- ok --> F[save tokens<br>+ open WS]
    C -- ok --> G[done]
    C -- fail --> H{email + password<br>available?}
    H -- yes --> E
    H -- no --> I[return False, reason]
    F --> G

docs.title: Three ways to authenticate
docs.text:
Email + passwordSaved tokens (auto)Manual access_token

First time only. Library saves the rotated tokens for next time. 

api = OlympTradeAPI(
    email="you@x.com",
    password="secret",
    mode="demo",
)
api.connect()

On second-and-after runs the library auto-loads saved tokens for email. Pass the same email — password becomes the fallback. 

api = OlympTradeAPI(
    email="you@x.com",
    password="secret",       # fallback if saved tokens fail
    mode="demo",
)
api.connect()                # uses saved tokens, no HTTP login

Skip everything else. Useful if you grab tokens from your browser's DevTools (Application → Cookies). 

api = OlympTradeAPI(
    access_token="eyJ...",
    refresh_token="eyJ...",  # optional but lets the lib auto-renew
    mode="demo",
)
api.connect()

docs.title: Where session files go
docs.text:
<your script's cwd>/olymp_<sha256(email)[:16]>.dat
  • Per-email — different accounts → different files, no collision
  • Filename hashed — your email never appears on disk
  • Encrypted — XOR + base64 (obfuscation, not strong crypto)

Add olymp_*.dat to your .gitignore

These files contain your access + refresh tokens. The repo's .gitignore already excludes them.

docs.title: Inspecting / clearing saved sessions
docs.text:
from olymptradeapi import session_store

# List all emails with saved sessions in this directory
session_store.list_saved_emails()       # ['alice@x.com', 'bob@y.com']

# Inspect the raw decrypted dict
session_store.load("alice@x.com")       # {'fp': {...}, 'tokens': {...}, 'email': '...'}

# Wipe a specific account's session
session_store.clear("alice@x.com")

docs.title: Auto-refresh (no captcha for 1+ year)
docs.text:
When the WS reconnects after a drop, the library tries the renew endpoint first. The new tokens are saved automatically. So a single email/password login gives you captcha-free service for the lifetime of the refresh_token (~1–3 years per the JWT exp claim).

You can also trigger it manually:

new_access = api.refresh_access_token()
print(f"new access token: ...{new_access[-16:]}")

docs.title: Friendly error messages
docs.text:
connect() returns (False, reason) with a clean reason string:

Reason returned Meaning Login returned HTTP 400: ... invalid_email_or_password wrong creds Login returned HTTP 422: ... wrong_captcha captcha — log in via browser once Token refresh returned HTTP 401: ... unauthorized refresh_token invalid; falls back to password if available

docs.title: Captcha workaround
docs.text:
If your IP / fingerprint gets captcha-flagged:

  1. Open https://olymptrade.com in Chrome
  2. Log in normally (solve the captcha there)
  3. F12 → Application → Cookies → https://olymptrade.com
  4. Copy access_token and refresh_token
  5. Pass them to OlympTradeAPI(access_token=..., refresh_token=...)

Once one captcha-free login completes, the saved-tokens path keeps you out of HTTP login forever.

docs.title: Balance
docs.text:
The library exposes balance through four methods that differ on two axes:

  • Single account (active mode only) vs all accounts (demo + real)
  • Cache (sub-millisecond, fed by WS pushes) vs HTTP (~150ms, ground truth)
Cache HTTP Active only get_balance() get_balance_http() All accounts api.api.balance (engine attribute) get_all_balances()

docs.title: The most common case
docs.text:
api = OlympTradeAPI(..., mode="demo")
api.connect()

print(api.get_balance().amount)        # demo live amount
api.change_account("real")
print(api.get_balance().amount)        # real live amount

get_balance() returns an AccountBalance object — see data models for the full field list.

docs.title: Live vs settled
docs.text:
OlympTrade reports two balance numbers in every push:

bal = api.get_balance()
bal.amount         # LIVE spendable — drops by stake the moment a trade opens
bal.amount_total   # SETTLED — only updates when the trade closes
bal.amount_real    # non-bonus portion (= amount on demo since no bonus)
bal.amount_free    # alias of amount
bal.holds_payout   # sum of pending payouts from open trades

bal.amount matches what the OlympTrade web UI shows on the top bar.

docs.title: When to use HTTP vs cache
docs.text:
Use the cache (get_balance()) when…

  • You only trade from this Python session
  • You want sub-millisecond reads
  • The values are kept fresh by WS e:55 pushes + the heartbeat

Use HTTP (get_balance_http()) when…

  • You also trade in the OlympTrade browser UI
  • You need ground truth (the WS cache is sometimes session-scoped)
  • You're building a dashboard and don't mind 150ms per call

docs.title: Polling examples
docs.text:
Cache poll (cheap, ~realtime)HTTP poll (authoritative, ~3s cadence)React on change only 
while True:
    print(api.get_balance().amount)
    time.sleep(0.5)

while True:
    print(api.get_balance_http().amount)
    time.sleep(3)

last_v = -1
while True:
    v = api.balance_version          # bumps on every WS push or HTTP refresh
    if v != last_v:
        last_v = v
        print(f"v{v}  ${api.get_balance().amount:.2f}")
    time.sleep(0.1)

docs.title: Multi-account
docs.text:
bal = api.get_all_balances()             # HTTP fetch, both accounts
print(f"demo: ${bal.demo.amount:.2f}")
print(f"real: ${bal.real.amount:.2f}")

docs.title: Switching the active account
docs.text:
api.change_account("real")               # sends e:184 + per-account subs
print(api.get_balance().amount)          # now returns real

change_account() also updates self._mode so subsequent get_balance() returns the right account automatically.

docs.title: Diagnosing "balance not updating"
docs.text:
If get_balance().amount looks stuck:

  1. Print api.balance_version — does it increment? If yes, server IS pushing, value just isn't changing. If no, see step 2.
  2. Server-idle timeout — happens if you don't send any frames for ~3 min. Default heartbeat (every 25s) prevents this. Don't set keepalive_interval=0 unless you know why.
  3. Session-scoped cache — if you trade in the browser, the Python WS may keep the pre-trade snapshot. Use get_balance_http() instead.

docs.title: Live callbacks
docs.text: The library is push-driven under the hood — every e:21 deal update that arrives is dispatched to any callback you've registered. Use this to react in real time without polling.

docs.title: on_deal_update
docs.text:
def on_upd(upd):
    print(f"deal={upd.deal_id} status={upd.interim_status} "
          f"price={upd.current_price} "
          f"interim_balance_change={upd.interim_balance_change}")

api.on_deal_update(on_upd)

Fires for every e:21 push, ~once per second per open deal.

docs.title: What upd carries
docs.text:
DealUpdate — a snapshot of the deal at this instant:

upd.deal_id                   # int
upd.interim_status            # "standoff" / "win" / "loose" (note: "loose" not "loss")
upd.current_price             # latest market price
upd.interim_balance_change    # what your P/L would be if it closed now
upd.is_win                    # bool helper
upd.is_loss                   # bool helper

# Convenience:
upd.is_settled                # True once the trade has actually closed

docs.title: Threading note
docs.text:
Callbacks fire on the WS reader thread. If you read shared state from the callback, protect it:

import threading

state_lock = threading.Lock()
last_status = {}                          # shared with the main thread

def on_upd(upd):
    with state_lock:
        last_status[upd.deal_id] = upd.interim_status

Don't time.sleep inside the callback — you'd block reception of every other push. Use a queue.Queue to hand off heavy work to a worker thread.

docs.title: Multiple callbacks
docs.text:
You can register as many as you want; they fire in registration order.

api.on_deal_update(log_to_disk)
api.on_deal_update(notify_telegram)
api.on_deal_update(update_dashboard)

docs.title: Realistic pattern: notify on settle
docs.text:
import threading

settled = threading.Event()
result_box = {}

def on_upd(upd):
    if upd.is_settled and upd.deal_id == r.deal_id:
        result_box["upd"] = upd
        settled.set()

api.on_deal_update(on_upd)

r = api.buy("EURUSD_OTC", 1, "up", 15)
settled.wait(timeout=20)
final = result_box["upd"]
print("WIN" if final.is_win else "LOSS")

This is essentially what check_win() does internally — use it directly unless you need the per-tick visibility.

docs.title: Candles
docs.text:
candles = api.get_candles(
    asset="EURUSD_OTC",
    size=5,                      # bar size in seconds (5, 30, 60, 300, ...)
    limit=600,                   # max candles to return
    to=None,                     # upper time bound (default: now)
)

Returns a list of dicts:

[
    {"t": 1777084600, "open": 1.1808, "low": 1.1807, "high": 1.1809, "close": 1.1808},
    {"t": 1777084595, "open": 1.1807, "low": 1.1806, "high": 1.1808, "close": 1.1808},
    ...
]

Most-recent candle is first in the list (descending time).

docs.title: Multiple timeframes
docs.text:
m1 = api.get_candles("EURUSD_OTC", size=60)        # 1-minute bars
m5 = api.get_candles("EURUSD_OTC", size=300)       # 5-minute bars
m15 = api.get_candles("EURUSD_OTC", size=900)      # 15-minute bars

docs.title: Historical range
docs.text:
import time
midnight = int(time.time()) - 60*60*24
candles = api.get_candles("EURUSD_OTC", size=60, to=midnight, limit=1440)
# 1440 1-minute candles ending at midnight = the full prior day

docs.title: Payouts (profitability per pair)
docs.text:
payouts = api.get_payouts()                 # {pair: percent}
print(payouts["EURUSD_OTC"])                # 85

Sort by payout to find the most attractive instruments:

top10 = sorted(payouts.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])[:10]
for pair, pct in top10:
    print(f"{pair:<14} {pct}%")

Most pairs sit at 80–90% payout during normal hours, with OTC pairs consistently at the top.

docs.title: Deal history
docs.text:
h = api.deal_history(limit=10)
for d in h["deals"]:
    print(f"{d['pair']:<14} {d['dir']:<4} {d['status']:<8} ${d['balance_change']:+.2f}")

Output:

EURUSD_OTC     up   loose    $-1.00
EURUSD_OTC     up   standoff $+0.00
EURUSD_OTC     up   win      $+0.85
AUDCHF_OTC     down win      $+0.85
GBPUSD         down loose    $-1.00

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
page1 = api.deal_history(limit=10)
page2 = api.deal_history(limit=10, cursor=page1["next_cursor"])
page3 = api.deal_history(limit=10, cursor=page2["next_cursor"])

The next_cursor is a base64-encoded {i:last_id, t:last_close_time_ms} that the server uses to continue paging.

docs.title: Filter by pair
docs.text:
# Only EURUSD_OTC deals
otc = api.deal_history(limit=20, pairs=["EURUSD_OTC"])

# Multiple pairs at once
fx = api.deal_history(limit=20, pairs=["EURUSD", "GBPUSD", "AUDUSD"])

docs.title: Asset lists (full instrument metadata)
docs.text:
ftt = api.list_ftt_assets()                # FTT instruments
fx = api.list_forex_assets()               # forex instruments

for a in ftt[:5]:
    print(f"{a.id:<14} payout={a.winperc}%  open={a.is_open}")

Each asset is a typed dataclass — see FTTAsset / ForexAsset / StockAsset.

docs.title: HTTP accounts list
docs.text:
for entry in api.list_accounts_http():
    acc = entry["account"]
    bal = entry["balance"]
    print(f"{acc['group']:<5} id={acc['id']:<12} ${bal['amount']:>10.2f}  {acc['name']}")

Output: 

real  id=1987976407   $      0.00   USD Account
demo  id=2746091247   $   9787.20   Demo Account

Useful before the WS connection comes up, or as a fallback when you only need the account list (no live updates).

docs.title: Place a Fixed-Time order
docs.text:
r = api.buy(
    asset="EURUSD_OTC",      # pair id from list_ftt_assets()
    amount=1,                 # stake (USD)
    direction="up",           # "up" or "down"
    duration=15,              # seconds
)

Returns an OrderResult — check r.ok first.

if not r.ok:
    print(r.error_code)       # e.g. "common_not_enough_real_funds"
    print(r.error_message)    # e.g. "Not enough real funds"
else:
    print(f"deal {r.deal_id} placed at strike {r.strike_price}")

docs.title: Two expiry modes
docs.text:
OlympTrade's FTT supports both timer-based (your stake closes N seconds after the order) and clock-based (closes at a specific epoch) trades. Pass exactly one of duration= or time_close=:

Timer (default OTC)Clock (regular FX/stocks) 
r = api.buy("EURUSD_OTC", 1, "up", duration=15)

import time
next_minute = int(time.time() // 60 + 1) * 60
r = api.buy("USDSGD", 1, "down", time_close=next_minute)

The reply differs in one field — is_time: false for timer, true for clock.

docs.title: Wait for the result
docs.text:
final = api.check_win(r.deal_id)
if final.is_win:
    print(f"WIN  +${final.interim_balance_change:.2f}")
elif final.is_loss:
    print(f"LOSS  ${final.interim_balance_change:.2f}")
else:
    print("DRAW")

check_win() blocks until close_time + settle_delay (default 2s) — you get back the latest DealUpdate state.

docs.title: Close a deal early
docs.text:
api.close_trade(r.deal_id)              # sends e:27

You'll get a partial refund based on OrderResult.cancel_percent. Useful when an indicator flips against you mid-trade.

docs.title: Pick the best-payout asset
docs.text:
payouts = api.get_payouts()             # {pair: percent}
top = sorted(payouts.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])[:5]
for pair, pct in top:
    print(f"{pair:<14} {pct}%")

Output: 

XRPUSD_OTC     90%
ETHUSD_OTC     90%
BTCUSD_OTC     90%
SOLUSD_OTC     90%
LTCUSD_OTC     90%

OTC pairs (weekend-only synthetic markets) often have higher payouts than regular FX during off-hours.

docs.title: Common error codes
docs.text: error_code Meaning Fix common_not_enough_real_funds Insufficient balance Top up, or trade less wrong_captcha Captcha challenge active Log in via browser to clear unauthorized access_token expired Library auto-refreshes; if it persists, re-login invalid_email_or_password Wrong creds Check env vars payout_changed Payout shifted between place and execute Retry, accept new payout

docs.title: Live deal updates (optional)
docs.text:
Register a callback to react to every e:21 interim update:

def on_upd(upd):
    print(f"deal {upd.deal_id}: {upd.interim_status} "
          f"(price {upd.current_price})")

api.on_deal_update(on_upd)

r = api.buy("EURUSD_OTC", 1, "up", 60)
api.check_win(r.deal_id)

The callback fires multiple times per trade (~once per second) on the WS reader thread.

docs.title: HTTP endpoints
docs.text:
All endpoints have been validated against live captures. Method is POST for all of them.

Endpoint Purpose Captcha-able? https://api.olymptrade.com/v2/user/login-by-password Email + password login :material-alert: yes https://gw.olymptrade.com/api/token/renew/web/v1 Refresh access_token :material-check-bold: no https://gw.olymptrade.com/api/accounts/list/v2 List accounts + balances no https://gw.olymptrade.com/api/storyly/profile User profile + labels no https://gw.olymptrade.com/api/history/deals/ftt/v1 FTT deal history no

docs.title: /v2/user/login-by-password
docs.text:
Request body:

{
  "list": ["data"],
  "data": {
    "email": "...",
    "password": "...",
    "dont_remember": false,
    "fp_id": "...",          // 32 lowercase hex chars
    "hardware_id": "hi_..."   // "hi_" + 32 url-safe base64 chars
  }
}

Response cookies set:

  • access_token — short-lived JWT (~48h)
  • refresh_token — long-lived JWT (1–3 years), path-restricted to /api/token/renew/web

docs.title: /api/token/renew/web/v1
docs.text:
Request: empty body, Cookie: refresh_token=eyJ...

Response: two Set-Cookie headers (clear old + set new) for both access_token and refresh_token. JSON body has {token_type, expires_in, recommended_refresh_in}.

The library handles paired Set-Cookie (the old cleared one + the new rotated one) correctly — see httpc/renew.py.

docs.title: /api/accounts/list/v2
docs.text:
Request:

{ "with_archive": true }

Response:

{
  "accounts": [
    {
      "account": {"id": ..., "group": "real", "type": "common", ...},
      "balance": {"amount": 0, "amount_free": 0, "amount_real": 0, ...}
    },
    ...
  ]
}

docs.title: /api/storyly/profile
docs.text:
Request: empty body.

Response: User metadata including custom_parameter (= user_id), labels (feature flags), and Storyly content tokens.

{
  "data": {
    "custom_parameter": "74007517",
    "labels": ["platform:web", "fiat", "ftt", ...],
    "token_main": "eyJ...",
    "token_help": "eyJ...",
    "user_property_data": {"url": "https://ul.olymptrade.com"}
  }
}

Doubles as an access_token health check — returns 401 if the cookie is expired/invalid.

docs.title: /api/history/deals/ftt/v1
docs.text:
Request:

{
  "cursor": "<base64>",      // optional, for pagination
  "limit": 10,
  "pairs": [],               // empty = all; or e.g. ["EURUSD_OTC"]
  "account_id": 2746091247
}

Response:

{
  "deals": [
    {
      "id": 12109774201,
      "pair": "EURUSD_OTC",
      "dir": "up",
      "status": "loose",
      "amount": 1,
      "balance_change": -1,
      "winperc": 85,
      "duration": 15,
      "curs_open": 1.18093, "curs_close": 1.18088,
      "time_open": 1777084472.731, "time_close": 1777084487.731,
      ...
    },
    ...
  ],
  "next_cursor": "eyJpIjox..."
}

next_cursor decodes to {i: <last_deal_id>, t: <close_time_ms>} — pass it back as cursor= to fetch older deals.

docs.title: Required headers (all gw.olymptrade endpoints)
docs.text:
Origin: https://olymptrade.com
Referer: https://olymptrade.com/
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 ...
X-Cid-App: web@OlympTrade@<version>@<build>
X-Cid-Device: @@desktop
X-Cid-Os: windows@10
X-Cid-Ver: 1
Cookie: access_token=eyJ...; refresh_token=eyJ...

The library sets all of these automatically — see constants.py for the cid values.

Do not send to gw.olymptrade.com:

  • X-Request-Project
  • X-Request-Type
  • X-Requested-With

These are accepted on api.olymptrade.com but rejected by the gw.* host with 400 bad_project_name. The library's httpc/renew.py has a comment on this — keep it that way if you fork.

docs.title: Protocol overview
docs.text:
OlympTrade speaks two protocols:

  1. HTTP for auth + history + accounts (api.olymptrade.com, gw.olymptrade.com)
  2. WebSocket for everything else, especially real-time pushes (ws.olymptrade.com)

The library mirrors this split:

olymptradeapi/
├── httpc/         ← HTTP resource classes
│   ├── login.py
│   ├── renew.py
│   ├── logout.py
│   ├── accounts.py
│   ├── profile.py
│   └── history.py
└── ws/
    ├── client.py        ← reader thread, dispatches frames
    ├── protocol.py      ← encode/decode JSON
    └── chanels/         ← outgoing channel classes (one per e-code)
        ├── auth.py
        ├── buy.py
        ├── candles.py
        ├── close_trade.py
        ├── get_asset_data.py
        ├── get_balance.py
        ├── payouts.py
        ├── ping_server.py
        ├── subscribe.py
        └── unsubscribe.py

Same architecture as pocketoptionapi.

docs.title: Wire format (WebSocket)
docs.text: Every frame is a JSON array wrapping one or more message objects.

docs.title: Outgoing (client → server)
docs.text:
[
  {
    "t": 2,                   // type: 2 = client request
    "e": 23,                  // event code
    "uuid": "MOD1YLM...",     // optional — server echoes back for replies
    "d": [                    // payload (always a list)
      { "amount": 1, "dir": "up", "pair": "EURUSD_OTC", ... }
    ]
  }
]

docs.title: Incoming (server → client)
docs.text:
[
  {
    "t": 3,                   // type: 3 = server reply (matched by uuid)
    "e": 23,                  // event code
    "uuid": "MOD1YLM...",     // matches the request
    "d": [{ "id": 12109..., "status": "proceed", ... }]
  }
]

[
  {
    "t": 1,                   // type: 1 = server push (no uuid)
    "e": 55,                  // event code (e:55 = balance)
    "d": [{ "account_id": 274..., "amount": 9787.20, ... }]
  }
]

docs.title: Type codes
docs.text: t Meaning 1 server push (unsolicited; no uuid) 2 client request 3 server reply (correlates by uuid)

docs.title: Subscription model
docs.text:
The browser subscribes to channels via e:98:

[{"t":2,"e":98,"d":[55, 74, 1054, 21, 22, 1076, 1097, 73, 182, 11]}]

After this, the server pushes events on those codes whenever they update (balance, instrument lists, deal updates, etc.).

The library does this once during connect() — see INITIAL_SUBSCRIPTION in constants.py.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• HTTP endpoints — full URL list with body shapes
  • WS events — every observed e: code

docs.title: WebSocket events
docs.text: Every e: code observed in live traces.

docs.title: Auth + meta
docs.text: e Direction Meaning Payload 14 both Server time / app-level keepalive {} (request); {st: epoch} (reply) 98 client Subscribe / unsubscribe to channels [event_codes]

docs.title: Identity / accounts
docs.text: e Direction Meaning Payload 184 both Switch active account [{account_id}] 31 both Per-account instrument auxiliary [{account_id, group}] 1043 both Per-account group config [{account_id, group}] 1068 both Per-account instrument config [{account_id, group}] 110 push User profile {...}

docs.title: Balance
docs.text: e Direction Meaning Payload 55 push Balance snapshot (per account) [{account_id, amount, amount_free, amount_real, holds, group, ...}] 54 push Wallet snapshot (older / less-used variant) [{account_id, amount, group}]

docs.title: Markets
docs.text: e Direction Meaning 74 push FTT instruments list 73 push FTT sentiment per pair 182 request/reply Payouts (profitability % per pair) 1076 push Digital options list (short FTT variants) 1054 push Forex CFD instruments 1097 push Forex sentiment per pair 2243 push Stocks ask price + min amount 2223 push Stocks instrument list

docs.title: Trading
docs.text: e Direction Meaning Payload 23 both Place a Fixed-Time order request: [{amount, dir, pair, cat, account_id, group, duration | time_close, ...}] 22 push Deal opened (mirrors e:23 reply) same shape as e:23 reply 21 push Deal interim update [{id, status, interim_status, current_price, ...}] 27 client Close deal early [{id, group}]

docs.title: Charts
docs.text: e Direction Meaning Payload 10 both Historical candles request: [{pair, size, to, limit}]; reply: [{p, tf, candles: [...]}] 11 push Per-pair server clock (candle-stream status) [{pair, st}]

docs.title: Notes on encoding
docs.text:
• Field name asymmetry: e:10 candles use pair / size in the request but p / tf in the reply.
  • Empty body for ping: e:14 sent as [{"t":2,"e":14,"uuid":"..."}] with no d.
  • Subscribe channels list 220, 101: occasionally seen in older traces; the modern initial subscribe set is (55, 74, 1054, 21, 22, 1076, 1097, 73, 182, 11) — defined in constants.INITIAL_SUBSCRIPTION.

docs.title: Where these are wired in the lib
docs.text: Code Outgoing (channel class) Incoming (handler) 10 ws/chanels/candles.py ws/client.py:_on_candles 11 – ws/client.py:_on_pair_clock 14 ws/chanels/ping_server.py – 21 – ws/client.py:_on_deal_update 22 – ws/client.py:_on_deal_opened 23 ws/chanels/buy.py (reply matched by uuid) 27 ws/chanels/close_trade.py – 31, 1043, 1068 ws/chanels/auth.py:SwitchAccount – 55 ws/chanels/get_balance.py ws/client.py:_on_balance 74, 1076 ws/chanels/get_asset_data.py ws/client.py:_on_ftt_list 98 ws/chanels/subscribe.py / unsubscribe.py – 182 ws/chanels/payouts.py ws/client.py:_on_payout 184 ws/chanels/auth.py:SwitchAccount – 1054 ws/chanels/get_asset_data.py ws/client.py:_on_forex_list 2243, 2223 ws/chanels/get_asset_data.py ws/client.py:_on_stocks / _on_stocks_list

docs.title: OlympTradeAPI
docs.text: The high-level user-facing class. Lives in olymptradeapi.stable_api (re-exported from the package root).

docs.text:
Returns (True, None) on success, (False, reason) on failure.

ok, reason = api.connect()

docs.text:
Closes the WS, joins the heartbeat / reconnect threads, closes the HTTP session.

api.logout()

docs.title: Internals (advanced)
docs.text:
If you need direct access to the engine:

api.api                                # the low-level olymptradeapi class
api.api.balance                        # raw multi-account Balance object
api.api.deals                          # dict[deal_id, DealUpdate]
api.api.deal_opened                    # dict[deal_id, OrderResult]
api.api.payouts                        # dict[pair, %]
api.api.candle_data                    # dict[(pair, tf), list-of-candles]

Channels are exposed as @property:

api.api.Buy(...)          # buy_digital channel
api.api.Subscribe([55])   # e:98 subscribe
api.api.Switch_Account(account_id, group, req_id)
api.api.Get_History(account_id, limit=10, cursor=None, pairs=None)
# ... etc

See Protocol overview for the full list.

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text: All exceptions are importable from olymptradeapi.

docs.title: Hierarchy
docs.text:
OlympTradeError                     base
├── AuthError                       login / refresh failures
├── ConnectionError                 WS upgrade / drop
├── NotConnectedError               called something before connect()
├── RequestError                    server replied with an error
└── RequestTimeout                  request didn't get a reply

docs.title: When you'll see them
docs.text: Exception Raised by Typical cause AuthError Login(), Renew() Invalid creds, expired refresh, captcha ConnectionError WSClient.connect() Server closed during upgrade NotConnectedError Any method that uses the WS Forgot to call connect() RequestError get_balance(), buy(), check_win(), ... No reply / bad data RequestTimeout WSClient.request() No reply within the configured timeout

docs.title: Pattern: handle auth failure cleanly
docs.text:
ok, reason = api.connect()
if not ok:
    print(reason)            # e.g. "Login returned HTTP 400: ..."
    raise SystemExit

connect() swallows AuthError and returns the reason as a string — no need to wrap it.

docs.title: Pattern: handle trade rejection
docs.text:
r = api.buy("EURUSD_OTC", 1000000, "up", 15)
if not r.ok:
    if r.error_code == "common_not_enough_real_funds":
        api.change_account("demo")     # try demo
        r = api.buy(...)
    else:
        log.error(f"buy rejected: {r.error_message}")

buy() returns an OrderResult with ok=False for all server-side rejections — no exception. RequestError is only raised for protocol-level failures (no reply, malformed data).

docs.title: Pattern: handle protocol timeout
docs.text:
from olymptradeapi import RequestTimeout

try:
    candles = api.get_candles("EURUSD_OTC", size=5, timeout=2.0)
except RequestTimeout:
    log.warning("server didn't return candles in 2s; skipping")
    candles = []

docs.title: Data models
docs.text: All dataclass-based, frozen-feel (the lib mutates them but you generally shouldn't). Importable from olymptradeapi.

docs.title: AccountBalance
docs.text:
Single-account snapshot.

Field Type Notes account_id int Unique per account group str "demo" or "real" amount float LIVE spendable (drops by stake on trade open) amount_total float Settled total (raw protocol amount) amount_real float Non-bonus portion amount_free float Same as amount (alias) holds_payout float Sum of pending payouts raw dict Original server payload 
bal = api.get_balance()
bal.amount          # 9779.53 — what the OlympTrade UI shows
bal.amount_total    # 9780.53 — only updates at settlement

docs.text:
Multi-account container.

Field/property Type Notes accounts list[AccountBalance] All accounts .demo AccountBalance? Demo (or None) .real AccountBalance? Real (or None) .by_id(account_id) AccountBalance? Lookup by id

docs.title: OrderResult
docs.text:
Returned by buy() / place_ftt(). The repr is concise (only populated fields).

Field Type Notes ok bool Trade accepted? deal_id int? Server-assigned id pair, direction, amount, duration various Echo of request account_id, group, currency various Account context status str? "proceed" / "closed" / ... interim_status str? "standoff" / "win" / "loose" winperc float? Payout % at place time cancel_percent float? Refund % if closed early open_price, strike_price float? curs_open / curs_strike current_price, close_price float? curs_current / curs_close open_time, close_time_planned, close_time float? epoch seconds is_flex, riskfree bool Variant flags balance_change, interim_balance_change float? P/L error_message str? Human-readable on failure (e.g. "Not enough real funds") error_code str? Machine-readable (e.g. "common_not_enough_real_funds") raw dict Full server reply 
r = api.buy(...)
if not r.ok:
    if r.error_code == "common_not_enough_real_funds":
        ...
print(r.full_repr())     # verbose form for debug logging

docs.title: DealUpdate
docs.text:
Pushed on every e:21 (interim deal status). Returned by check_win().

Field Type Notes deal_id int? pair, direction, amount, duration various status str? interim_status str? "standoff" / "win" / "loose" current_price float? curs_current interim_balance_change float? What P/L would be if it closed now balance_change float? Final P/L (set after settle) time_open, time_close float? epoch seconds raw dict Property Returns is_win bool is_loss bool (note: server sends "loose") is_settled bool (status moved off "proceed")

docs.title: FTTAsset / ForexAsset / StockAsset
docs.text:
Returned by list_ftt_assets() / list_forex_assets() / list_stock_assets().

for a in api.list_ftt_assets():
    print(a.id, a.winperc, a.is_open, a.group)

Common fields:

Field Type Notes id (or ticker for stocks) str Pair / ticker group str? "otc" / "forex" / etc winperc float Payout % (FTT only) is_open bool Currently tradable raw dict Full instrument metadata

Stocks additionally expose ask_price and ask_min_amount.

docs.title: session_store
docs.text:
The per-email encrypted session persistence module.

from olymptradeapi import session_store

docs.title: Module functions
docs.text: Function Returns Notes load(email) dict Decrypted session, or {} if missing/corrupt save(email, data) None Atomic write update(email, *, fp=None, tokens=None) dict Merge-update clear(email) None Delete the file file_for(email) Path The on-disk path for this email store_dir() Path Currently Path.cwd() list_saved_emails() list[str] Scans cwd for olymp_*.dat

docs.title: On-disk shape
docs.text:
<cwd>/olymp_<sha256(email)[:16]>.dat

  • Per-email — multiple accounts coexist
  • Hashed name — email never appears on disk
  • Encrypted — XOR + base64 (obfuscation, not strong crypto)

Decrypted contents:

{
    "email": "alice@x.com",
    "fp": {"fp_id": "...", "hardware_id": "..."},
    "tokens": {
        "access_token": "eyJ...",
        "refresh_token": "eyJ...",
    },
}

docs.title: When the lib reads/writes the file
docs.text: Action Reads Writes OlympTradeAPI.__init__(email=...) ✅ (loads saved fp + tokens for this email) – connect() succeeds via password – ✅ (saves new tokens) connect() succeeds via tokens – ✅ (re-saves) refresh_access_token() succeeds – ✅ (saves rotated tokens) change_account() – –

docs.title: Disable persistence
docs.text:
OlympTradeAPI(email=..., password=..., persist_session=False)

No file gets written. Useful for ephemeral / test contexts.

docs.title: Manual interaction
docs.text:
InspectWipe one accountWipe everything 
state = session_store.load("alice@x.com")
print(state.keys())                    # dict_keys(['email', 'fp', 'tokens'])
print(state["tokens"]["access_token"][:30])

session_store.clear("alice@x.com")

for email in session_store.list_saved_emails():
    session_store.clear(email)

docs.title: ⚠️ Security note
docs.text:
The XOR key is hard-coded in the source (so this is obfuscation, not encryption). The threat model is:

  • :material-check: Casual filesystem snooping (anyone reading olymp_*.dat in a text editor sees random bytes)
  • :material-check: Accidental copy-paste of a token
  • :material-close: A determined attacker with code access — they can decrypt

For production, store credentials in a real secret manager (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, etc.) and pass them explicitly via env vars.
